 ReactOS finally adds USB 3.0 support after years of development
 The open-source Windows alternative ReactOS now includes USB 3.0 drivers.
 Nov 7, 10:33 GMT • WhyCry • 2 min read Set as Preferred Source Follow on Google Open-source Windows alternative receives USB 3.0 drivers in latest nightly builds
 ReactOS has added its first USB 3.0 driver stack after several years of development. The open-source operating system, which aims to run Windows applications and drivers without using Microsoft’s Windows kernel, now includes support for xHCI USB controllers in its latest nightly builds.
 The update was announced on November 6 by the ReactOS team. Developer Justin Miller, known as DarkFire01, contributed three drivers: USBHUB3, USBXHCI and UCX01000. These components provide the foundation for USB 3.x controller support, extending the operating system beyond its previous USB 1.1 and USB 2.0 implementations.
 BREAKING NEWS: USB 3.0 age on #ReactOS has just started!
 After years of efforts, our developer @The_DarkFire__ has added USB3 stack drivers (USBHUB3, USBXHCI and UCX01000) into our latest nightly builds. We are excited to see the effects!!
 — ReactOS (@reactos) November 6, 2026 
 The code was merged into the main ReactOS repository through pull request #9646. Miller explained that the driver stack had undergone multiple revisions over several years. He also tested the implementation on Windows 11 systems, replacing Microsoft’s USB stack with his own drivers. According to the developer, the implementation has been stable during his testing.
 © Github The new stack also prepares ReactOS for USB4 development. Miller says a separate pull request will add USB4 host and device router support after the required DeviceProperty functionality is integrated. The current implementation also includes hardware-specific workarounds for controllers used in Qualcomm and NVIDIA SoCs, with provisions for ARM32 and ARM64 support.
 USB 3.0 support is currently available through development builds rather than the stable ReactOS 0.4.16 release, which launched in August. 
 I’ve never actually tried ReactOS. I guess Linux gaming has improved so much over the years that I never really felt the need to. What about you? Have you ever given ReactOS a try, even in a virtual machine?
